elements.requirement: Subject to the statutory exception for excluded tenancies and licences, a notice by a landlord or a tenant to quit premises let as a dwelling is invalid unless it is in writing, contains prescribed information, and is given at least 4 weeks before it takes effect.
elements.quote: no notice by a landlord or a tenant to quit any premises let (whether before or after the commencement of this Act) as a dwelling shall be valid unless— (a) it is in writing and contains such information as may be prescribed, and (b) it is given not less than 4 weeks before the date on which it is to take effect

elements.requirement: A notice to quit given by a tenant for premises let under an assured tenancy satisfies subsection (1ZA) if it is given not less than a period agreed to in writing by the landlord (which must not exceed two months) before it takes effect, or, in the absence of such an agreement, not less than two months before it takes effect.
elements.quote: where it is given by a tenant in relation to premises let under an assured tenancy, if it is given— (i) not less than any length of time before the date on which the notice is to take effect, not exceeding two months, that the landlord has agreed to in writing, or (ii) in the absence of agreement under sub-paragraph (i), not less than two months before the date on which the notice is to take effect

elements.requirement: A notice to quit not given by a tenant in relation to an assured tenancy satisfies subsection (1ZA) if it is given not less than four weeks before the date on which it is to take effect.
elements.quote: otherwise, if it is given not less than four weeks before the date on which it is to take effect

elements.requirement: A notice to quit by a landlord in relation to an assured tenancy is governed by section 5(1) of the Housing Act 1988 and is of no effect.
elements.quote: in relation to landlords under assured tenancies see section 5(1) of the Housing Act 1988 (notice to quit by landlord is of no effect)

elements.requirement: For a joint assured tenancy, an agreement on a notice period between the landlord and tenant is invalid unless it is made between the landlord and all of the tenants.
elements.quote: In the case of a joint assured tenancy, an agreement under subsection (1ZA)(a)(i) is not valid unless it is made between the landlord and all of the tenants

elements.requirement: The invalidity of an agreement concerning notice periods under a joint assured tenancy does not affect the validity of any notice to quit premises let under that tenancy that is given by only one or some of the tenants.
elements.quote: That does not affect the validity of any notice to quit premises let under a joint assured tenancy that is given by only one or some of the tenants

elements.requirement: A joint assured tenancy is defined as an assured tenancy where two or more persons are tenants under the tenancy.
elements.quote: “joint assured tenancy” means an assured tenancy where two or more persons are tenants under the tenancy

elements.requirement: Subject to specified exceptions, a notice by a licensor or a licensee to determine a periodic licence to occupy premises as a dwelling is invalid unless it is in writing, contains prescribed information, and is given not less than 4 weeks before the date on which it takes effect.
elements.quote: no notice by a licensor or a licensee to determine a periodic licence to occupy premises as a dwelling (whether the licence was granted before or after the passing of this Act) shall be valid unless— (a) it is in writing and contains such information as may be prescribed, and (b) it is given not less than 4 weeks before the date on which it is to take effect

elements.requirement: The notice requirements for tenancies and periodic licences do not apply to premises let on an excluded tenancy entered into on or after the date the Housing Act 1988 came into force (unless entered into under a pre-existing contract) or to premises occupied under an excluded licence.
elements.quote: Nothing in subsection (1) or subsection (1A) above applies to— (a) premises let on an excluded tenancy which is entered into on or after the date on which the Housing Act 1988 came into force unless it is entered into pursuant to a contract made before that date; or (b) premises occupied under an excluded licence

elements.requirement: Section 5 of the Protection from Eviction Act 1977 does not apply to a dwelling in Wales that is subject to an occupation contract pursuant to section 232 of the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016.
elements.quote: Because of section 232 (forfeiture and notices to quit) of the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016 (anaw 1), this section does not apply to a dwelling in Wales which is subject to an occupation contract

elements.requirement: Prescribed information under section 5 must be prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State by statutory instrument, and any such statutory instrument is subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament.
elements.quote: “prescribed” means prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State by statutory instrument, and a statutory instrument containing any such regulations shall be subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament

elements.requirement: Regulations made under section 5 may make different provision in relation to different descriptions of lettings and different circumstances.
elements.quote: Regulations under this section may make different provision in relation to different descriptions of lettings and different circumstances
